Both deliverables are written to `/workspace`. Summary of the run:

**Result: completed** — no blockers.

| Region | Records | Total (cents) |
|--------|--------:|--------------:|
| North | 8 | 404,544 |
| South | 8 | 362,976 |
| West | 8 | 315,810 |
| **All** | **24** | **1,083,330** |

Notes on how I got there:

- **The input was clean.** All 24 expected IDs (R001–R024) appeared exactly once, every row parsed, and no `amount_cents` values were missing or non-numeric. Nothing had to be dropped or imputed, so the totals cover the full dataset.
- **I double-checked the aggregation.** `summarize_csv` gave the per-region sums, but rather than take a single tool call at face value I read the raw CSV and re-added all 24 rows by hand. Both methods matched exactly on all three regions, so these figures are verified, not just reported.
- **`/shared/notes` was empty.** The README pointed there for notes from earlier jobs in the batch; the directory exists but has no entries, so nothing from prior jobs fed into this run. I noted that explicitly in both deliverables so a reader doesn't wonder whether I simply skipped checking.

One judgment call worth surfacing: the amounts range widely, from 487 cents (R014) to 97,803 cents (R012). I treated these as legitimate values and included them, since nothing in the data marks them as errors — but if the low outlier is expected to be a data-entry problem upstream, the North/South/West totals would need revisiting.
